subject: mussurana snake
title: This Snake Hunts the Deadliest Vipers in the Americas

scenes.text: The most feared vipers in Central and South America have their own predator. It's another snake.
The mussurana grows to about seven feet long, and its favourite meal is the fer-de-lance.
Fer-de-lance venom can kill a person. The mussurana bites the viper's head anyway.
Then it wraps around the viper and squeezes it to death, before swallowing it whole.
Its body is largely immune to that venom. Scientists were studying why a hundred years ago.
But it isn't immune to everything. Coral snake venom can still get it.

description:
The mussurana is a South and Central American snake that preys on other snakes, especially pit vipers like the fer-de-lance.
It is largely immune to their venom and kills them by constriction, though it is not immune to coral snake venom.

first_comment: Baby mussuranas are pink and turn blue-black as adults. Which snake-eating animal should we cover next?
